# Ordinary writable TMPFS shared-memory regression

Checkpoint59 bounded regression. The fixture-only build and53 synthetic offline codec checks have passed; **no Guest or VM execution has occurred**. The primary contract is `goals/progress/39/contract-59-writable-tmpfs.md`. This separate fixture does not change the checkpoint58 readonly fixture, shared headers, CMake, production code or disk topology. Its validator qualifies only a complete offline protocol; kernel/artifact/VM identity, init-service completion, storage admission and physical cleanup remain external runner obligations.

## Claim and decisive negative

The controller uses actual `shm_open` in a private `/dev/shm` mount view. Data Files use ordinary O_RDWR/O_RDONLY flags, including libc's normal CLOEXEC behavior, **without O_NO_CACHE**. Only the separate report/control File uses O_NO_CACHE. The same prefilled O_RDONLY description is read sequentially, sought back, and read again after acknowledged mapped writes. `pread` is not substituted for this cache-authority test: current VFS deliberately excludes positional reads from the stream cache.

The first substantive oracle is a mapped store observed by a pre-existing independent O_RDWR alias in a fork root and then by the prefilled ordinary reader. All read-only mappings are deliberately created after the initial writable/store/VFS-read checks. This lets the genuine checkpoint58 RAW implementation reach the copied-alias/cache oracle before its separate ordinary-RO-map admission refusal. The old negative must compile/run this exact fixture and preserve its actual failure prefix; no deliberately wrong queue or mapping algorithm is substituted. The source was genuinely compiled for WOS; neither a current-kernel Guest run nor the genuine old-RAW runtime negative has occurred yet. The synthetic old-RAW/cache negatives test decoder sensitivity only.

## Actual processes and bounded phases

The Host coordinator runs as UID/GID100, creates one actual private compartment through the existing CREATE ABI, and inherits only a regular control File at FD9. The private controller is local PID1. It forks child2; that child unmaps the inherited writable alias and independently maps the same object at another fixed vacant VA. Child2 later forks exit-only descendant3, exactly reaps it, closes its data FDs and execs the same private asset. The replacement still has local PID2 and parent1; it checks data FDs are closed and kernel copy-from the old VA fails, then exits0. No thread or synthetic current Task is involved. The Host exactly reaps the private controller.

1. Create `/dev/shm/writeshared-probe`, EOF=4169 (PAGE+73), with exact nonce-derived marker/complement and73-byte final-page prefix. Ordinary RO FD11 is fully sequentially read before any mapping. The controller maps ordinary RW FD10 at `0x4000000000`, opens a separate writer FD12, closes FD10 and reuses10 for the unrelated control File. Captured mappings must keep the original object; F_GETFL before/after admission must be unchanged.
2. Child2 unmaps the inherited alias and opens/maps the same named object RW at `0x5000000000`. The controller stores tag2, child reads its existing alias and ACKs, then the prefilled reader must see tag2. Ordinary pwrite tag3 must appear in both independent roots and the same reader. Child then stores tag4, ACKs, and controller existing map plus ordinary reader must see tag4. Each read follows a completed control handoff; overlapping reads are not used as sequential-coherence proof.
3. Only now map the ordinary RO File at `0x4100000000`. Whole RW -> READ -> NONE -> RW transitions must succeed. Kernel copy-to a READ map and copy-from a NONE map must each return -EFAULT without changing guarded data; restored RW admits tag5. O_RDONLY WRITE mapping/promotion and either-description EXEC mapping/promotion return -EACCES. Typed MS_SYNC=4, MS_ASYNC=1, SYNC|INVALIDATE=6 succeed; unknown8 and contradictory SYNC|ASYNC=5 return -EINVAL. No RAW copy-to-self oracle is accepted in place of the earlier visibility checks.
4. Grow while owners live returns -EBUSY and retains exact EOF. Controller writes0xa5 only in the final-page padding `[4169,8192)`. Child opens an independent ordinary RO map at `0x5100000000` after the synchronized writes, observes tag5, publishes READY and makes one bounded real FUTEX_WAIT on its aligned word128. Controller stores tag6 and wakes the matching word through its different-VA RW alias. Exactly one wake succeeds, WAIT returns0, and child reads tag6 before ACK. Polling, timeout or zero-only wake earns no credit.
5. Descendant3 reads both inherited child aliases and exits0. Child2 exactly reaps it and execs with its mappings still present so real exec retires them; replacement checks the old fixed VA is inaccessible to usercopy, then exits0. Controller exactly reaps child2, unmaps both of its maps, and retries ordinary grow for the scoped EOF lease to disappear. Grow must eventually succeed, preserve the last73 visible bytes and all other expected bytes, and expose all4023 previously tainted padding bytes as zero. This is a scoped tail/EOF-release witness, **not** proof of callback RETURNED, global frame/reference balance or all-owner drains.

Every error path preserves available committed reports, kills/reaps only its exact known child when necessary, and relies on actual process/namespace exit as the remaining map/FD backstop. No manual kernel callback, File operation table, private GC call or modeled backing is used.

## Fixed artifacts and protocol

The future runner creates `/srv/tmpfs-writeshared-results` as mode0700 owned100:100 and installs the executable at `/usr/libexec/compartment-tmpfs-writeshared-runtime`; private assets are `/app/writeshared-probe`, `/lib/ld.so`, `/usr/lib/libc.so`. The executable starts in Host mode with no arguments. Internal controller/new-image modes require the exact decimal nonce/deadline and, for exec, the old fixed VA. The separate real init-status witness service invokes the same Host executable with `--init-exit-witness` as UID/GID100 and targets service `tmpfs-writeshared-probe`. It polls the actual init ABI for at most30s, saves `init-exit-status`512B and `init-exit-snapshot.bin`4160B, and prints the exact successful status line once. No new ABI is introduced.

The base70-event protocol uses exactly seven files:

| File | Bytes | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `host.bin` |4096|Host CREATE/reap report|
| `role-1.bin` |4096|private controller|
| `role-2.bin` |4096|independent child before exec|
| `role-3.bin` |4096|replacement image|
| `role-4.bin` |4096|normal-exit descendant|
| `control.bin` |32768|actual command/ACKs, guarded failed-copy scratch and report copies|
| `status` |512|exact PUBLIC_COMPLETE line plus zero padding|

Each report is512 little-endian uint64 words. Header words0..37 contain magic/version/role, common nonce/deadline, actual local PID/PPID, monotonic interval, failure count/first stage, observation count, actual File identity/access flags, map geometry, child/physical CREATE IDs, control identity, credentials, shape and target msync constants. Reserved words are zero;62/63 are guards. Observations start64, ten words each: opcode, local sequence, monotonic time, a/b, signed result and three concrete values, then guard. Capacity44; unused words are zero and final word511 is nonce commit. Successful counts are exactly `[2,44,17,2,5]`,70 observations total. The validator checks every operation/result/value and ordering, not a bitmap or PASS string.

Control records are512-byte guarded, double-read messages at offsets0(startup),512(child initial-ready),1024(final command3),1536(final ACK3),2048(futex-ready). Scratch4096..4127 must remain `{guard,0,0,~guard}`. Role copies are at `8192+role*4096`, roles1..4; unused control bytes, including role0's unused slot, must be zero. Each report/message is written with a zero commit, fsynced, then committed and fsynced. The final host.bin is saved independently after private-controller reap.

The strict decoder takes a report directory and returns COMPLETE_OFFLINE_WRITESHARED_PROTOCOL_ONLY with `vm_identity_qualified=false` and `public_runtime_qualified=false`. `--diagnostic` decodes available fixed-size failure prefixes and always exits nonzero; it never supplies missing roles or success. Source/ELF/kernel identity and raw artifact readback qualification must be added by a separately reviewed runner. The runner must also retrieve both actual witness files, call the exported strict `init_snapshot(snapshot,status)` decoder, and match host.bin PID word5 to the actual init serial spawn before Guest success. Thus full runner qualification requires all nine files; the seven-file base `decode` result alone proves no init exit. The adapted58 witness and decoder preserve real generation1/restart0/EXITED/READY/wait0/history/zero-padding checks; no modeled transition replaces them.

## Bounds, future execution and limits

Guest work has a60s absolute monotonic deadline and5s per handshake/wait/reap/grow window; wake attempts<=128 and grow attempts<=64. Data is two pages, control32KiB, five reports20KiB, status512B. A future runner must preserve one exact-owned topology, immutable shared seeds/private COW images,20GiB disposable budget/40GiB free floor, the original protected VM/shared launch guard, exact owned stop/FD/backing proofs and all-outcome pruning/postcheck. `--no-setup` does not waive those checks. This program creates no Host images.

No full POSIX mmap, all-filesystem writeback/durability, actual SMP futex stress, cross-compartment SysV handle grant, arbitrary resize/remap or1000-cycle/2h claim is made. The current work includes actual repo format-only, a bounded fixture-only compile/link with complete emitted input pins and an ELF gate, and53 synthetic decoder checks (one full raw positive,51 targeted negatives, one failure-prefix nonqualification). Sources held and private compile/codec scratch was removed. The real init-exit witness source is a functional03 addition requiring its own fresh build and synthetic snapshot checks before use. Genuine old/current Guest execution, physical admission and all-outcome VM cleanup remain future coordinator actions; synthetic success supplies none of that credit.
